# Curated guard shell regressions

## Scope and provenance

These fixtures pin mechanisms under a **synthetic config**, not the
user-config-specific measurements. Those remain in
[the design document](../../../docs/guard-design.md#shell-ast-adoption-final-measurement-and-retirement-record).

Collected from the final code on 2026-11-06. Source hashes identify commands
in the second full decision-diff run (09:50 UTC): 34,969 real commands plus
11 synthetic inputs. The temporary measurement harness and raw outputs were
deleted after preserving the measurements in the design document.

- `hard.json`: 83 cases: all 11 rejected corpus commands, six manual-wrapper
  specimens, six formerly ambiguous compounds, six redirect-aware specimens,
  the five false-allow constructions and six malformed inputs, plus 43
  focused mechanism/construct cases.
- `widening.json`: all 43 reviewed tier-recovery commands, in full except for
  path/identifier replacement. Synthetic-policy results: 38 allow, five
  prompt. The five prompts lack the original user's git/gh/dynamic-path
  rules; they are not silently granted synthetic rules to replay the old
  measurements.
- `incompleteness.json`: 69 run-2 incompleteness specimens. Prefer the
  shortest representative per fingerprint (command head plus separators,
  substitutions, redirects, multiline forms), not near-duplicate rows for
  every changed cell. At most eight per cause, hard cap 20:
  - `background`: 8
  - `command-substitution`: 8
  - `function-definition`: 8
  - `grouped`: 8
  - `heredoc`: 8
  - `process-substitution`: 8
  - `state-change`: 5
  - `subshell`: 8
  - `unrecognized-node`: 8

The test is `tests/guard-shell-fixtures.test.mts`, in both `test:ci` and
`test:guard`. `tests/guard-shell-fixture-policy.mts` owns the small policy
and observation helper. Each run creates a fresh temp directory.
`{{CWD}}`, `{{READ}}`, `{{WRITE}}`, and `{{OUTSIDE}}` resolve to distinct
children. Config roots and command placeholders use the SAME mapping.
`{{ITEM_ID}}` resolves to an inert synthetic identifier. Windows home
paths and vault identifiers/accounts are also replaced. Nothing executes;
no user guard.json, real classifier, or credentials are used. Paths in
historical command bodies are data, not live source references.

Synthetic rules exercise plain allow, redirect-aware allow, ask, deny, and
Pwsh allow. `HostBash(echo *)` deliberately cannot authorize an incomplete
substitution or a non-exempt write redirect.

## Assertions and review

Each row pins ACTION, adapter machine cause, and matched rule identifier
(null if no rule decided), plus every step's action, adapter cause, matched
rule, and redirect-awareness gate. `complete` means the AST projection is
complete, NOT safe; `not-bash` denotes the whole-command Pwsh path.
Neither code is derived from reason prose. Rule IDs come from the
evaluator's additive `matchedRule` metadata, not rule re-matching or prose
parsing. Aggregate metadata belongs to the decisive step.

Expectations were generated by the final evaluator, then reviewed against
all step reasons, unwrapped argv, explicit rules, assignment semantics,
and profile cells. Do not blindly regenerate them. A fresh temp-root run
verified substitution independently of the collection root.

### Matched allow rule (3)

- `plain-allow`
- `redirect-allow`

### Pure assignment (1)

### Permissive profile cell (4)

- `yolo-incomplete`
- `trusted-cell`
- `unrestricted-cell`
- `pwsh-trusted-cell`

No-op cd names the synthetic cwd. Write-root, /dev/null, and descriptor
redirects are documented tier exemptions, not accidental gate bypasses.
`yolo-incomplete` pins the accepted whole-command yolo behavior: an inner
ask rule is not a raw whole-command match and is not rediscovered inside
an unrepresentable group. `ask-before-yolo` prompts and
`deny-before-yolo` denies.
